oliver: hi all, oliver here — quick question while setting up my dev env. Should I be using a hosted API key or the sandbox key for local testing? What's the difference in limits and billing?

natalie: welcome! use the sandbox key for dev and exploratory work. Hosted keys are for prod (they're tied to org billing). Sandbox is rate/usage limited and sits behind shared onboarding credits.

oliver: thanks — where do I get the sandbox key? I only see a generic API keys page.

infra-bot: Notice: New hire accounts should have a SANDBOX key auto-created. Check Console > Settings > API keys > "Sandbox". If missing, run `cat ~/.redwood/keys.json` or open a #help ticket with subject: "sandbox key missing: <your-email>".

oliver: found it, thanks. Any idea what the default rate limits look like? Trying to plan a demo script.

ryan: defaults vary a bit, but expect ~50-80 requests/min and ~4 concurrent requests typical for sandbox. Token/day caps are applied (soft) for new orgs. If your demo needs sustained throughput, ask for a temporary bump.

oliver: how do I ask? link or form?

natalie: file a request via the intranet form: https://intranet.redwood.ai/onboarding/quota. Choose "sandbox temporary increase" and include: expected qps, duration, and test plan. Platform team usually approves same day for short demos.

oliver: cool. Do sandbox calls show up on our billing statement if I accidentally run a big test? Don't want to charge prod cards.

ryan: sandbox is on onboarding credits and won't hit your org billing. We still monitor and cap abusive/very heavy usage. For anything close to production load, use a hosted key with proper billing or request Dedicated.

oliver: for demos I'm doing streaming responses — any gotchas?

natalie: streaming uses connections and counts toward concurrent connection limits. Keep parallel streams low (<=4) or you'll hit socket limits. Also backoff on 429/503. Example basic retry header you can use client-side:
```
// pseudocode
if (resp.status == 429) wait = base * 2**attempt + jitter; retry();
```

infra-bot: Tip: For local development you can set REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY in your env and use `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY" https://api.sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/chat`

oliver: perfect, thanks. One last: can I get a hosted key scoped to a sandbox-like quota for a team sandbox project?

ryan: we can create a hosted key under a test billing profile and apply custom quotas, but that needs approvals. For quick stuff use the normal sandbox bump route. If you need a recurring higher baseline, talk to your manager and we can route to sales/devops for a test org setup.

oliver: awesome. appreciate the fast responses :raised_hands:
